description: Perturbative necessity/sufficiency campaign for exact detector-degeneracy activation versus wrapped heavy-tailed P(theta). It combines clean Ising and non-pure-Ising SU(2)-exchange cases, hz0=0, collective Jx=0.01, edge coupling Jx/sqrt(N), and t=1e6. Zero parameters are admitted as exact symmetry limits; every nonzero |hz|, |J|, and |Jpm| is at least 10 Jx.

cases.rationale: Exact zero-scale symmetry limit: all detector states are degenerate and D_act=1, but the finite-N phase law is atomic rather than a resolved heavy tail.
Exact zero-field Ising resonance with D_act=1/2 and J/Jx=100.
Exact local spin-flip resonance at hz=+2J with D_act=1/4; all physical scales exceed collective Jx by at least 100x.
Spin-reversed exact local resonance at hz=-2J with D_act=1/4; all physical scales exceed collective Jx by at least 100x.
A 0.01 detuning removes exact activation (minimum coupled gap 0.02), while N=14 remains heavy-tailed.
Spin-reversed 0.01 detuning removes exact activation while preserving a perturbative field scale.
Far from all exact Ising spin-flip resonances; tests that absence of activation can also coincide with a non-heavy distribution.
Non-pure-Ising SU(2) exchange: at hz=0, [H_D,V]=0 and all V weight is exactly degenerate, while J/Jx=50 and Jpm/Jx=100. The finite-N P(theta) is expected to remain atomic.
Non-pure-Ising SU(2) exchange at the smallest admitted perturbative scales. Since hz is nonzero, every V transition has gap 2|hz| and exact activation is absent.
Non-pure-Ising SU(2) exchange with intermediate J and Jpm; exact activation is rigorously absent at nonzero hz.
Strong non-pure-Ising SU(2) exchange control; Jx is at most one percent of hz, J, and Jpm, and exact activation is absent.
